prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” HVAC company for every Atlanta homeowner — the right choice depends on your neighborhood, budget, system needs, timing, and whether you prioritize lowest price, longest warranty, brand installers (Carrier/Trane/etc.), or fast emergency service. I can, however, help you choose a top-quality contractor and shortlist good candidates in your area.

Quick plan I recommend
1. Give me your ZIP code (or neighborhood) and a few details (home square footage, age of current system, budget or brand preference). I’ll pull a short list of highly rated local companies and current typical pricing ranges.
2. Get 3 written, comparable estimates (same scope, same equipment) so you can compare.
3. Choose a contractor that checks the boxes below (licenses, certifications, good references, clear warranty/permit policy).

What to look for (must-haves)
- Georgia HVAC license and local permits: contractor should handle permits and code compliance.
- NATE-certified technicians or equivalent training.
- Good local reviews (Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB) and verifiable references.
- Detailed written estimate with equipment make/model, SEER rating, labor warranty, and removal/disposal of old unit.
- Performs a Manual J load calculation (not just “size by rule of thumb”).
- Offers manufacturer AND labor warranties; get those in writing.
- Clear payment/financing options and start/completion dates.
- Proper refrigerant handling (R-22 vs R-410A) — replacement considerations if you have an older unit.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see your license number and COI?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation?
- What brand/models do you recommend and why? What SEER will I get?
- What’s included in labor and parts warranty? Any prorated manufacturer warranty?
- Do you handle permits and inspections?
- Will you provide a written estimate with line-item costs?
- Can you provide recent local references?

Red flags
- High-pressure sales or “today-only” discounts.
- Vague estimates or refusal to put scope in writing.
- No willingness to do load calculations or provide references.
- Extremely low bids without explanation of differences.

How I can help right now
- If you share your ZIP code (and any preferences: brand, budget, timing), I’ll give a tailored shortlist of 3–5 highly rated Atlanta HVAC companies, plus what to expect on price and timeline.
- I can also provide a comparison checklist/template to evaluate any quotes you receive.

Would you like me to find top-rated companies near you? If so, tell me your ZIP code and any priorities (brand, budget, warranty).
